classification.difficultyReason: Translate between inequalities, interval notation and number-line graphs by identifying endpoint inclusion and ray direction. The hardest row requires reading two disconnected graph components and expressing their union; all conversions directly apply the taught conventions.

answer.worked: Include $-3$ with a square bracket and exclude $5$ with a round bracket: $[-3,5)$.
Both endpoints are closed, so both are included: $-1\le x\le3$, or $[-1,3]$.
$2$ is excluded and the interval continues indefinitely to the right. Infinity is always excluded: $(2,\infty)$.
The interval extends left indefinitely and includes $3$: $(-\infty,3]$.

answer.short: $x<4$. Open endpoint at $4$, ray to the left.
answer.worked: The round bracket excludes $4$. Draw an open endpoint at $4$ and a ray extending left to represent $x<4$.

answer.short: $x\ge5$. Closed endpoint at $5$, ray to the right.
answer.worked: The square bracket includes $5$. Draw a closed endpoint at $5$ and a ray extending right to represent $x\ge5$.

answer.worked: The open endpoint excludes $-2$ and the ray selects smaller values: $x<-2$, or $(-\infty,-2)$.
$x<1$ gives $(-\infty,1)$ and $x\ge3$ gives $[3,\infty)$. Join the intervals with $\cup$: $(-\infty,1)\cup[3,\infty)$.
Include $-1$ and $2$ with square brackets and join the two intervals: $(-\infty,-1]\cup[2,\infty)$.
Exclude $-4$, include $-1$, and include $3$ in the rightward interval. Infinity is excluded: $(-4,-1]\cup[3,\infty)$.
The leftward ray excludes $-3$, giving $x<-3$. The segment includes both $0$ and $2$, giving $0\le x\le2$. Together: $(-\infty,-3)\cup[0,2]$.

inlines.text: A square bracket or closed endpoint includes the boundary; a round bracket or open endpoint excludes it. Infinity always has a round bracket. A union joins the separate intervals.
